action_text: I walk into Ashfall Village at dusk, the blade heavy at my hip.
narration_text: Ashfall smells of wet ash long after the fires stopped. The few lit windows watch you pass. At the end of the main street a lantern hangs over the door of the Ember Inn, and a bent figure is wiping the same table for the third time.

action_text: I step into the inn and ask for a bed.
narration_text: The woman behind the bar looks you over. "Old Marta," she says, pointing a thumb at herself. "Bed's four coppers, stew is free if you keep your boots off the benches." The room is nearly empty, and the hearth burns low.

action_text: I ask Marta who guards the road to the cairn.
narration_text: "The Vigil, what's left of them." She jerks her head toward the gate. "Captain Ose runs it now. Captain Ose keeps the gate key on a cord around his neck, and he sleeps with one hand on it."

action_text: I ask Marta how long she has run the inn.
narration_text: "Old Marta keeps the Ember Inn at the end of the main street, and has since before the fires," she says, and the pride in it is thin as paper. "My husband Hale built the counter. The cairn took him the year the well went dry."

action_text: I thank her and reach for my coins to pay for the stew.
narration_text: Marta waves the coins away and, with a sudden stubborn generosity, presses a purse of three hundred gold crowns into your hand. The weight of it surprises you, and she will not meet your eye.

action_text: I ask her about her husband.
narration_text: Her chin trembles once. "Hale," she says. "He carried the family lantern into the cairn the night it took him. Nobody has seen it since." She goes back to the table and wipes it again, harder this time.

action_text: I go up to the gate and look over the Vigil.
narration_text: Two sentries stand at an iron-bound gate under a slate sky. Brother Tam, a boy in a patched Vigil cloak, is trimming the lamps with a hooked pole. Brother Tam keeps the gate lamps burning through the night, and his hands are black to the wrist with soot.

action_text: I stop and talk to Brother Tam.
narration_text: Tam glances at the sentries, then slips a folded letter out of his cloak. "For the Warden," he whispers, and presses it into your palm. You look at his shaking hands and give your word: you promise Brother Tam that you will carry his letter to the Warden.

action_text: I go to find Captain Ose.
narration_text: Captain Ose is a broad man with a tired face. He studies your blade, then the sky. "Go in if you must," he says. "I swear the Vigil will hold the gate until you come back out." It sounds like an oath he has said before.

action_text: I look for Kestrel Vane and ask him to guide me.
narration_text: Kestrel Vane is sitting on a barrel by the stable. Kestrel Vane carries a crooked bow of ash wood, and he does not look up from oiling it. "I know the cairn," he says finally. "I was a Vigil apprentice. I'll show you the entrance, no further." Something in his shoulders loosens when you do not argue.

action_text: I sharpen the Rustbound Blade by the stable lantern.
narration_text: The blade is plain and a little rusted along the fuller, but it takes an edge. Kestrel watches the whetstone work. "Better than bare hands," he mutters, which from him is a compliment.

action_text: I ask Marta whether anything stirs in the village at night.
narration_text: A bell begins to toll from the gate, three slow strokes and a pause. Marta bolts the shutters. "Alarm," she says. "Somebody saw lights on the hill." The village goes quiet as a held breath, and every street is emptied by the order of the bell.

action_text: I drink the bitter tonic Marta brews for the road.
narration_text: The tonic tastes of tar and honey. You feel your health rise to one hundred and fifty, as if the village itself were breathing into you, and the ache in your shoulders goes away.

action_text: I climb the hill road and look up at the cairn.
narration_text: The Hollow Cairn squats on the hill like a sunken tooth. For a moment the dark in its mouth leans toward you, as if it had been waiting. Far above, something that is not wind turns its head.

action_text: I go back down and check my pack by the fire.
narration_text: Rope, flint, a heel of bread. Marta's stew has settled warm in your stomach. Kestrel sits across from you, silent, mending a bowstring in the firelight, and the village sleeps behind its shutters.

action_text: I ask Kestrel why he left the Vigil.
narration_text: "The Vigil guards the outside of the cairn," he says. "It never learned what to do about the inside." He pulls the string tight and does not say more, and the fire pops into the quiet.

action_text: I walk the village wall at dawn.
narration_text: Gray light crawls over the roofs. The sentries are changing, and nobody looks at the hill. At dusk the iron barrier is lowered across the hill road, and the road to the cairn is closed after dusk on the captain's order.

action_text: I ask a sentry who holds the east watch.
narration_text: "Captain Ose holds the east watch himself," says the sentry, "and trusts it to nobody." Ose, overhearing, only grunts. The alarm bell has gone quiet, and the bells will not ring again tonight.

action_text: I test the blade on a fence post.
narration_text: The Rustbound Blade bites into the post and sticks. When you wrench it free a flake of rust falls away, and the edge looks a shade duller. When you turn around, Kestrel's bedroll by the stable is empty and cold.

action_text: I follow the hill road to the cairn and step inside.
narration_text: The air inside is cold and smells of wet ash. The entrance closes behind you the way a mouth closes. Somewhere deeper, a slow sound like breathing carries through the stone.

action_text: I light a torch and move down the passage.
narration_text: The torchlight reaches only a few paces. The walls are carved with small repeating hands, each one pressing outward from the inside. You try not to count them.

action_text: I draw the blade and hold it up to the carvings.
narration_text: The carvings seem to flinch. In your grip the Rustbound Blade turns to pure silver, bright as a mirror, and the hands on the wall pull back.

action_text: I follow the passage to a great door.
narration_text: The passage ends at a door twice your height. The Choir Door is sealed with a ring of black iron, and from behind it comes a low chorus of voices that stop when you stop.

action_text: I press my ear to the door and listen.
narration_text: The voices are not words. They are the shape words leave behind, like the print of a hand in ash. Your torch gutters though there is no draft.

action_text: I search the side chambers.
narration_text: Dust, bones, and a broken stool. The air of the cairn smells of wet ash even here, a long way from any fire. In a niche you find a child's shoe, very old, very small.

action_text: I move on, following a draft of colder air.
narration_text: The passage slopes down. Water ticks somewhere, and the stone underfoot turns damp. At the foot of the slope a shape lies against the wall, bound and still.

action_text: I try the Choir Door again.
narration_text: You lay your palm on the iron ring and the Choir Door swings open on its own, silent on its hinges. Beyond it lies a long hall full of waiting dark, and the voices begin again.

action_text: I cut the bonds of the figure by the wall.
narration_text: It is Kestrel Vane, gray with cold, an arrow-wound in his thigh and his bow gone. "You came in," he says hoarsely. "Fool." But he grips your arm hard. The door above you has not moved; the iron ring is still sealed.

action_text: I bind his wound and help him sit.
narration_text: He is shaking, and he hates it. "I owe you a debt, Wren," he says. "I will not forget it." You wrap the wound with your own scarf and he lets you.

action_text: I search the altar niche and read the carvings.
narration_text: The altar's inscriptions slide into sense under your fingers. In the hall beyond the sealed door, something pale sits hunched over the stone, and it is not breathing. Beneath that blank gaze you lay Brother Tam's letter on the altar, and the letter lies at the Warden's feet and your promise to Brother Tam is kept.

action_text: I ask Kestrel whether he has any way to break the seal.
narration_text: Kestrel reaches inside his coat and brings out a warded relic, a palm-sized disc with three embers glowing in its heart. "The Ember Sigil," he says, and presses it into your hand. You touch it to the black iron ring. One ember burns down to ash and the ring glows red, and the voices beyond scream once and stop.

action_text: I rest while Kestrel's wound closes.
narration_text: Kestrel sleeps sitting up, one hand on his knife. You keep watch on the dark and the dark keeps watch on you. Your torch burns down a finger's width.

action_text: I wake Kestrel and ask what he knows of the Warden.
narration_text: "It never speaks first," Kestrel says. "It watches. It remembers everyone who walks in, and it keeps what they are most afraid to lose." He looks at the Ember Sigil in your hand and looks away.

action_text: I listen for the horn Kestrel says he heard.
narration_text: Far above, a horn sounds three falling notes. Kestrel goes pale. "The gate is abandoned," he says. "Captain Ose has broken his oath to hold the gate." The notes die in the stone, and neither of you speaks for a while.

action_text: I scout the passage beyond the altar.
narration_text: The passage narrows and turns, and the carved hands give way to carved faces, each with its mouth open. The torch shows only the nearest, then the next, then the dark.

action_text: I check on Kestrel after the rockfall.
narration_text: A slab has come down behind you and the dust is still settling. You find Kestrel sitting in the rubble, bleeding from the scalp, and for a long second you think the worst: Kestrel Vane dies of his wounds in the dark, and the world narrows to the sound of dripping water. Then he coughs, furious, and sits up.

action_text: I help Kestrel up and thank him for the warning.
narration_text: "Don't thank me," he says, leaning on you more than he would like. "Get us out." For the first time he calls you by name without sneering, and he keeps his hand on your shoulder a moment longer than he needs to.

action_text: I step into the hall and speak to the Warden's still shape.
narration_text: The shape does not turn. Its voice, when it comes, is the sound of ash settling. "I will seal this cairn at dusk and you will not leave it," it says, and the doors of the hall breathe shut one by one.

action_text: I hold up the Ember Sigil to show the Warden what I carry.
narration_text: The embers in the disc flare, and the carvings on the walls turn their faces toward it. The Ember Sigil gains five new charges, or so it seems to the light, which pulses brighter than before.

action_text: I press the sigil to the seal again, harder.
narration_text: The ring of black iron glows red, then white, then runs like wax down the face of the door. The ring of black iron has melted away and the Choir Door is unsealed, and the voices behind it fall silent all at once.

action_text: I step through the Choir Door into the hall of voices.
narration_text: The hall is long and low, lined with the faces of everyone the cairn ever kept. At the far end the Warden has lifted its head. It has noticed you now, truly, and the walls begin to weep something dark and slow.

action_text: I ask Kestrel what he found out about the captain.
narration_text: Kestrel produces a crumpled page torn from a Vigil ledger, stained brown at the edges. It lists payments, season after season, in Ose's own hand, each marked with the cairn's sign. "He was on the inside of this for years," Kestrel says quietly. "Nobody on the outside knew."

action_text: I breathe in and taste the hall.
narration_text: The smell has changed. The air of the cairn now smells of burning pine, sharp and clean, as if the sigil had scoured it. Your lungs ache with the unfamiliar sweetness of it.

action_text: I search the base of the altar for another way out.
narration_text: Behind the altar you find a drain in the floor and, beside it, a loose stone. For one dizzy moment the light bends and the Warden's health drops to zero, and the hall holds its breath. Then the Warden's head turns, and it is plainly still standing, watching you like a hand on the back of your neck.

action_text: I turn to find where the noise came from.
narration_text: A slab breaks free of the ceiling above you. Kestrel does not think. Kestrel Vane repays his debt by shoving you clear of the falling stone, and the slab takes his bow arm instead of your head. He swears, for a long time, in several languages.

action_text: I look through the loose stone and see what lies behind it.
narration_text: Behind the stone there is a shaft that falls away to dark water, and in the water, a bundle wrapped in oilcloth. Kestrel reaches for it with his good arm. "The old well," he says. "The Ash Well runs under the whole hill. The captain kept coming here for this."

action_text: I use the Ember Sigil to light the shaft.
narration_text: The sigil burns down another ember and the shaft lights from within, showing the bundle clearly. The light dies slowly, as if reluctant to go, and the Warden's eyes follow it.

action_text: I hold the sigil between me and the Warden and do not move.
narration_text: A long silence. The Warden's blank face tilts, and the walls stop weeping. The Warden withdraws its threat to seal the cairn, with a sound like a sigh, and the hall breathes open again.

action_text: I lift the oilcloth bundle out of the water.
narration_text: The bundle is heavy and sodden. Inside, wrapped in wax paper, is a thin book of accounts, the pages swollen with damp. Kestrel turns them with a fingertip. "Names," he says. "Dates. Sums."

action_text: I strike the Rustbound Blade against the drain grate.
narration_text: The grate shrieks and gives. The Rustbound Blade has gone dull and notched from the work, and the tang is loose in the hilt. It will do for one more fight, perhaps.

action_text: I show Kestrel the first page of the book.
narration_text: The page is a list of dates and sums with a single name at the top of every column: Ose. Kestrel reads in silence, then closes the book very gently. "I used to think he was only tired," he says.

action_text: I ask the Warden what it wants.
narration_text: The Warden does not answer. It lifts one hand, and in the palm there is a small, soot-black lantern, the kind Marta described. The light inside it has not gone out in all these years.

action_text: I look at the Warden's face by the lantern's light.
narration_text: The face is worn almost smooth, but at the brow a scar is visible, a scar you have seen before on a boy at the village gate. The Warden watches you recognize it and does not look away.

action_text: I cross the hall and stand in front of the Warden.
narration_text: It is taller than it looked from the door, and it is old. It holds the lantern out, and when you take it the weight is more than a lantern ought to weigh. Somewhere above, a bell begins to ring.

action_text: I rest my hand on the lantern and breathe out.
narration_text: A warmth spreads through you and the cold lifts: your sanity is fully restored to one hundred, and the carved faces on the walls seem to nod. Kestrel watches you with the expression of a man doing arithmetic.

action_text: I ask Kestrel how long we have before the way closes.
narration_text: "Hours," Kestrel says. "Maybe less. The hall is different now. Faster." He tests his arm and winces. "Whatever you plan to do, plan to do it standing up."

action_text: I lay the book of accounts on the altar.
narration_text: The pages stir without wind. The Warden bends over them and reads slowly, the way the very old read, one finger on each line. Its face does not change, but the lantern in your hand burns a little lower.

action_text: I wait and watch the Warden finish the book.
narration_text: The Warden straightens. It looks at the Ember Sigil, at Kestrel, at you. Nobody has said a word in a long time. The bell above has stopped, and the dust has stopped, and even the water in the shaft is quiet.

action_text: I ask the Warden to let Kestrel pass.
narration_text: The Warden considers this for so long that the lantern's light steadies and the hall settles around it. Then it steps aside from the altar, which is as close to an answer as it has ever given anyone.

action_text: I take Kestrel's good arm and walk toward the way out.
narration_text: The passage ahead is lit with a faint, clean light. The carved faces turn as you pass, one after another, and none of them has its mouth open any more. Behind you the Warden stays where it is, as it always has.
